title: Initial speed calculation
description: Essential: The student must correctly derive and state the initial speed entering the electric field as √(2qEL/m).

title: Electric field kinematics
description: Important: The student must apply projectile motion equations in the electric field, relating horizontal displacement (2L) and vertical displacement (L) to time, acceleration (qE/m), and initial speed.

title: Velocity at point b
description: Important: The student must correctly compute the speed and direction (45° angle) of the particle at point b by combining horizontal and vertical velocity components.

title: Magnetic force for circular motion
description: Essential: The student must apply Newton's second law for circular motion (qvB = mv²/R) to relate magnetic field strength, speed at b, and trajectory radius.

title: Geometry for reaching point c
description: Important: For part (2)(I), the student must establish the geometric condition (n * 2R = √2 L) for the particle's circular arc to pass from b to c after multiple half-cycles.

title: Discrete magnetic field values
description: Essential: For part (2)(I), the student must combine the geometry and force law to give the final answer B = 2n√(2mE/qL) with n = 1, 2, 3...

title: Geometry for avoiding cd region
description: Important: For part (2)(II), the student must analyze the trajectory geometry to find the radius conditions (e.g., 2R > 3√2 L/2) that prevent the particle from reaching the cd segment.

title: Magnetic field range
description: Essential: For part (2)(II), the student must correctly state the final range for B, either as B < (4/3)√(2mE/qL) or as 2√(2mE/qL) < B < (8/3)√(2mE/qL).

title: Sign or unit error
description: Pitfall: Deduct points for sign errors in electric/magnetic force direction, incorrect unit handling, or misidentifying the charge's sign in the Lorentz force.

title: Incorrect collision assumption
description: Pitfall: Penalize assuming a single half-circle trajectory for part (2)(I) without considering multiple n, or misinterpreting the 'bc = 2cd' geometry for part (2)(II).
